# 1. Introduction

This report links previously detected outlier SNPs to genome annotation features.

For each outlier SNP, the report identifies:

genes directly overlapping the SNP;
the nearest gene when the SNP is intergenic;
distance to the nearest gene;
gene identifiers and annotation attributes extracted from the GFF/GTF file;
candidate gene lists for downstream functional annotation with tools such as `eggNOG-mapper` or `InterProScan`.

# 2. Packages

## 2.1. Install packages

```{r}
packages_cran <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "janitor",
  "readr"
)

for (pkg in packages_cran) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}

packages_bioc <- c(
  "GenomicRanges",
  "IRanges",
  "rtracklayer"
)

for (pkg in packages_bioc) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    BiocManager::install(pkg)
  }
}

```

## 2.2. Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

library(GenomicRanges)
library(IRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
```

Need to be adapted for the species (AND, BOM, LML)

```{r}
outlier_file_3plus <- file.path(

)

outlier_file_3plus
annotation_file
```

## 4.1 Read outlier tables

```{r}
outliers_raw <- read_csv(
  outlier_file_3plus,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  clean_names()

glimpse(outliers_raw)
names(outliers_raw)

# checks that the expected columns exist
required_outlier_cols <- c(
  "chr",
  "pos",
  "snp_id",
  "bay_pass_c2",
  "bay_pass_bf",
  "baye_scan",
  "pc_adapt",
  "bay_pass_local_scores",
  "n_methods",
  "overlap_category"
)

missing_outlier_cols <- setdiff(required_outlier_cols, names(outliers_raw))

if (length(missing_outlier_cols) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing expected columns in outliers_raw: ",
    paste(missing_outlier_cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# standardize column names
outliers <- outliers_raw %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    CHR = dplyr::all_of("chr"),
    POS = dplyr::all_of("pos"),
    SNP_ID = dplyr::all_of("snp_id")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    CHR = as.character(CHR),
    POS = as.numeric(POS),
    SNP_ID = as.character(SNP_ID)
  )

glimpse(outliers)

nrow(outliers)
n_distinct(outliers$SNP_ID)
```

## 4.2. Read genome annotation file

```{r}
annotation_gr <- rtracklayer::import(annotation_file)

annotation_gr
table(annotation_gr$type)

# The object annotation_gr is a GRanges object containing all annotation features

```

## 4.3. Extract genes

```{r}
# This keeps only annotation features of type "gene"
genes_gr <- annotation_gr[annotation_gr$type == "gene"]

genes_gr
length(genes_gr)

if (length(genes_gr) == 0) {
  stop("No features with type == 'gene' were found in the annotation file.")
}
```

## 4.4. Harmonise chromosome names

outlier_table - CHR1, CHR2, etc
gtf_file - 1, 2, etc

This is necessary because findOverlaps() only works if the SNP and gene coordinates use the same chromosome names.

```{r}
gtf_chrs <- unique(as.character(seqnames(genes_gr)))

outliers_mapped <- outliers %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    CHR_original = CHR,
    CHR = stringr::str_remove(CHR, "^CHR")
  )

cat("Outlier chromosome examples before mapping:\n")
print(head(unique(outliers$CHR), 30))

cat("\nMapped outlier chromosome examples:\n")
print(head(unique(outliers_mapped$CHR), 30))

cat("\nGTF chromosome examples:\n")
print(head(gtf_chrs, 30))

cat("\nNumber shared after mapping:", length(intersect(unique(outliers_mapped$CHR), gtf_chrs)), "\n")

outliers_mapped <- outliers_mapped %>%
  dplyr::filter(CHR %in% gtf_chrs)

cat("Rows after mapping:", nrow(outliers_mapped), "\n")
cat("Unique SNPs after mapping:", dplyr::n_distinct(outliers_mapped$SNP_ID), "\n")

if (nrow(outliers_mapped) == 0) {
  stop("No AND outlier chromosomes matched the annotation after chromosome harmonisation.")
}

```

## 4.3. Convert outliers/genes to GenomicRanges

This converts SNPs into genomic intervals

Each SNP becomes a 1 bp interval

This is the object used for genomic overlap analysis

```{r}
# Convert outliers to GenomicRanges
outlier_gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
  seqnames = outliers_mapped$CHR,
  ranges = IRanges::IRanges(
    start = outliers_mapped$POS,
    end = outliers_mapped$POS
  ),
  SNP_ID = outliers_mapped$SNP_ID
)

outlier_gr

# Convert gene annotation to table
genes_table <- as_tibble(genes_gr) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    CHR = as.character(seqnames),
    gene_start = start,
    gene_end = end,
    gene_strand = as.character(strand)
  )

glimpse(genes_table)
```

# 5. Extract gene IDs from GTF

This section standardises gene identifiers

```{r}
extract_first_available_column <- function(df, candidates) {
  
  available <- candidates[candidates %in% names(df)]
  
  if (length(available) == 0) {
    return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(df)))
  }
  
  df[[available[1]]]
}

genes_table <- genes_table %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_id = extract_first_available_column(
      .,
      c("gene_id", "id", "gene", "locus_tag", "name")
    ),
    
    gene_name = extract_first_available_column(
      .,
      c("gene_name", "gene", "name", "product")
    ),
    
    gene_description = extract_first_available_column(
      .,
      c("description", "product", "note", "gene_biotype")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_id = as.character(gene_id),
    gene_name = as.character(gene_name),
    gene_description = as.character(gene_description)
  )

genes_table %>%
  dplyr::select(
    CHR,
    gene_start,
    gene_end,
    gene_strand,
    gene_id,
    gene_name,
    gene_description
  ) %>%
  head()
```

# 6. Find outlier SNPs overlapping genes

Which outlier SNPs physically fall inside gene coordinates?

relation_to_gene = "overlapping"
distance_to_gene = 0

```{r}
overlap_hits <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(
  query = outlier_gr,
  subject = genes_gr,
  ignore.strand = TRUE
)

overlap_hits
length(overlap_hits)

if (length(overlap_hits) > 0) {
  
  outlier_gene_overlaps <- tibble(
    outlier_index = queryHits(overlap_hits),
    gene_index = subjectHits(overlap_hits)
  ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      outliers_mapped[.$outlier_index, ] %>%
        dplyr::select(CHR, CHR_original, POS, SNP_ID, everything())
    ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      genes_table[.$gene_index, ] %>%
        dplyr::select(
          gene_chr = CHR,
          gene_start,
          gene_end,
          gene_strand,
          gene_id,
          gene_name,
          gene_description
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      relation_to_gene = "overlapping",
      distance_to_gene = 0
    )
  
} else {
  
  outlier_gene_overlaps <- tibble(
    CHR = character(),
    CHR_original = character(),
    POS = numeric(),
    SNP_ID = character(),
    gene_chr = character(),
    gene_start = numeric(),
    gene_end = numeric(),
    gene_strand = character(),
    gene_id = character(),
    gene_name = character(),
    gene_description = character(),
    relation_to_gene = character(),
    distance_to_gene = numeric()
  )
}

glimpse(outlier_gene_overlaps)

n_distinct(outlier_gene_overlaps$SNP_ID)
n_distinct(outlier_gene_overlaps$gene_id)
```

# 7. Find nearest gene for all outlier SNPs

This section finds the nearest gene to every outlier SNP

This produces a nearest gene for each SNP, even if the SNP is intergenic

```{r}
nearest_gene_index <- GenomicRanges::nearest(
  x = outlier_gr,
  subject = genes_gr,
  ignore.strand = TRUE
)

nearest_gene_table <- outliers_mapped %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    nearest_gene_index = nearest_gene_index
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(nearest_gene_index)) %>%
  bind_cols(
    genes_table[.$nearest_gene_index, ] %>%
      dplyr::select(
        nearest_gene_chr = CHR,
        nearest_gene_start = gene_start,
        nearest_gene_end = gene_end,
        nearest_gene_strand = gene_strand,
        nearest_gene_id = gene_id,
        nearest_gene_name = gene_name,
        nearest_gene_description = gene_description
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    distance_to_nearest_gene = dplyr::case_when(
      CHR != nearest_gene_chr ~ NA_real_,
      POS >= nearest_gene_start & POS <= nearest_gene_end ~ 0,
      POS < nearest_gene_start ~ nearest_gene_start - POS,
      POS > nearest_gene_end ~ POS - nearest_gene_end,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    relation_to_nearest_gene = dplyr::case_when(
      distance_to_nearest_gene == 0 ~ "overlapping",
      distance_to_nearest_gene > 0 ~ "intergenic_nearest",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

glimpse(nearest_gene_table)

n_distinct(nearest_gene_table$SNP_ID)
n_distinct(nearest_gene_table$nearest_gene_id)
```

# 8. Build candidate gene table

Which genes are associated with my strongest outlier SNPs?

For intergenic SNPs, only keep the nearest gene if it is within 50 kb.

```{r}
nearest_gene_distance_threshold <- 50000

overlapping_snp_ids <- unique(outlier_gene_overlaps$SNP_ID)

intergenic_nearest_genes <- nearest_gene_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(!SNP_ID %in% overlapping_snp_ids)

candidate_genes_from_overlaps <- outlier_gene_overlaps %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    CHR,
    CHR_original,
    POS,
    SNP_ID,
    candidate_gene_id = gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name = gene_name,
    candidate_gene_description = gene_description,
    candidate_gene_chr = gene_chr,
    candidate_gene_start = gene_start,
    candidate_gene_end = gene_end,
    candidate_gene_strand = gene_strand,
    relation_to_gene = "overlapping",
    distance_to_gene = 0
  )

candidate_genes_from_nearest <- intergenic_nearest_genes %>%
  dplyr::filter(distance_to_nearest_gene <= nearest_gene_distance_threshold) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    CHR,
    CHR_original,
    POS,
    SNP_ID,
    candidate_gene_id = nearest_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name = nearest_gene_name,
    candidate_gene_description = nearest_gene_description,
    candidate_gene_chr = nearest_gene_chr,
    candidate_gene_start = nearest_gene_start,
    candidate_gene_end = nearest_gene_end,
    candidate_gene_strand = nearest_gene_strand,
    relation_to_gene = paste0("nearest_within_", nearest_gene_distance_threshold / 1000, "kb"),
    distance_to_gene = distance_to_nearest_gene
  )

candidate_gene_table <- bind_rows(
  candidate_genes_from_overlaps,
  candidate_genes_from_nearest
) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    SNP_ID,
    candidate_gene_id,
    relation_to_gene,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(CHR, POS, distance_to_gene)

glimpse(candidate_gene_table)

n_distinct(candidate_gene_table$SNP_ID)
n_distinct(candidate_gene_table$candidate_gene_id)
```

## 8.1 Add method-support information

This section adds back the outlier-detection method information

This SNP is linked to this candidate gene, and this SNP was supported by X methods

```{r}
method_columns <- c(
  "bay_pass_c2",
  "bay_pass_bf",
  "baye_scan",
  "pc_adapt",
  "bay_pass_local_scores",
  "n_methods",
  "overlap_category"
)

available_method_columns <- method_columns[method_columns %in% names(outliers_mapped)]

available_method_columns

candidate_gene_table_full <- candidate_gene_table %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    outliers_mapped %>%
      dplyr::select(SNP_ID, dplyr::any_of(available_method_columns)),
    by = "SNP_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_methods), CHR, POS, distance_to_gene)

glimpse(candidate_gene_table_full)
```

```{r}
candidate_gene_ids <- candidate_gene_table_full %>%

    n_nearest_gene_records = sum(str_detect(relation_to_gene, "^nearest_within_"), na.rm = TRUE),
```

# 10. Candidate summary

Summary report

## 10.1. Gene-level

This is very important for interpretation because the SNP-level table can contain repeated genes

For example, several SNPs may point to the same gene

This is probably the best pre `eggNOG` table for biological interpretation

```{r}
candidate_genes_gene_level <- candidate_gene_table_full %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    candidate_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name,
    candidate_gene_description,
    candidate_gene_chr,
    candidate_gene_start,
    candidate_gene_end,
    candidate_gene_strand
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_outlier_snps = n_distinct(SNP_ID),
    snps = paste(unique(SNP_ID), collapse = "; "),
    original_chromosomes = paste(unique(CHR_original), collapse = "; "),
    positions = paste(unique(POS), collapse = "; "),
    relation_types = paste(unique(relation_to_gene), collapse = "; "),
    min_distance_to_gene = suppressWarnings(min(distance_to_gene, na.rm = TRUE)),
    max_method_support = suppressWarnings(max(n_methods, na.rm = TRUE)),
    overlap_categories = paste(unique(overlap_category), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    desc(max_method_support),
    desc(n_outlier_snps),
    min_distance_to_gene,
    candidate_gene_chr,
    candidate_gene_start
  )

candidate_genes_gene_level

write_csv(
  candidate_genes_gene_level,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_genes_gene_level_summary.csv")
  )
)

# This counts how many candidate genes came from each relation type
candidate_genes_relation_summary <- candidate_genes_gene_level %>%
  dplyr::count(
    relation_types,
    name = "n_candidate_genes"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_candidate_genes))

write_csv(
  candidate_genes_relation_summary,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_genes_relation_summary.csv")
  )
)

# This counts candidate genes by maximum method support
candidate_genes_method_support_summary <- candidate_genes_gene_level %>%
  dplyr::count(
    max_method_support,
    name = "n_candidate_genes"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(max_method_support))

write_csv(
  candidate_genes_method_support_summary,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_genes_method_support_summary.csv")
  )
)

```

## 10.2. Feature-level

Is the SNP in a transcript?
Is it in an exon?
Is it in a CDS?
Is it in a start codon or stop codon?

```{r}
feature_types_to_check <- c(
  "gene",
  "transcript",
  "mRNA",
  "exon",
  "CDS",
  "five_prime_utr",
  "three_prime_utr",
  "five_prime_UTR",
  "three_prime_UTR",
  "start_codon",
  "stop_codon"
)

# Classify the functional genomic context of each SNP
feature_gr <- annotation_gr[annotation_gr$type %in% feature_types_to_check]

table(feature_gr$type)

feature_hits <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(
  query = outlier_gr,
  subject = feature_gr,
  ignore.strand = TRUE
)

length(feature_hits)

```

### 10.2.1. Convert feature overlaps to a table

This table can have multiple rows per SNP because one SNP may overlap several annotation features

For example, one SNP could overlap:

gene
transcript
exon
CDS

```{r}
feature_table <- as_tibble(feature_gr) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    feature_chr = as.character(seqnames),
    feature_start = start,
    feature_end = end,
    feature_strand = as.character(strand),
    feature_type = type
  )

if (length(feature_hits) > 0) {
  
  snp_feature_annotation <- tibble(
    outlier_index = queryHits(feature_hits),
    feature_index = subjectHits(feature_hits)
  ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      outliers_mapped[.$outlier_index, ] %>%
        dplyr::select(
          CHR,
          CHR_original,
          POS,
          SNP_ID,
          n_methods,
          overlap_category
        )
    ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      feature_table[.$feature_index, ] %>%
        dplyr::select(
          feature_type,
          feature_chr,
          feature_start,
          feature_end,
          feature_strand,
          dplyr::any_of(c(
            "gene_id",
            "transcript_id",
            "id",
            "parent",
            "gene_name",
            "gene_biotype",
            "protein_id",
            "product",
            "description",
            "note"
          ))
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      CHR_original,
      POS,
      feature_type,
      feature_start
    )
  
} else {
  
  snp_feature_annotation <- tibble(
    CHR = character(),
    CHR_original = character(),
    POS = numeric(),
    SNP_ID = character(),
    n_methods = numeric(),
    overlap_category = character(),
    feature_type = character(),
    feature_chr = character(),
    feature_start = numeric(),
    feature_end = numeric(),
    feature_strand = character()
  )
}

write_csv(
  snp_feature_annotation,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_outlier_SNPs_feature_level_annotation.csv")
  )
)

```

### 10.2.2. Summarise feature types per SNP

This collapses the feature-level table to one row per SNP

This is useful to identify SNPs with stronger functional relevance

SNP in CDS > SNP in intron > SNP intergenic, with the caveat that regulatory regions can also be important

```{r}
if (nrow(snp_feature_annotation) > 0) {
  
  snp_feature_summary <- snp_feature_annotation %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene_id = if ("gene_id" %in% names(.)) gene_id else NA_character_,
      transcript_id = if ("transcript_id" %in% names(.)) transcript_id else NA_character_,
      gene_name = if ("gene_name" %in% names(.)) gene_name else NA_character_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      SNP_ID,
      CHR_original,
      CHR,
      POS,
      n_methods,
      overlap_category
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      feature_types = paste(sort(unique(feature_type)), collapse = "; "),
      gene_ids = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(gene_id))), collapse = "; "),
      transcript_ids = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(transcript_id))), collapse = "; "),
      gene_names = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(gene_name))), collapse = "; "),
      in_gene = any(feature_type == "gene"),
      in_transcript = any(feature_type %in% c("transcript", "mRNA")),
      in_exon = any(feature_type == "exon"),
      in_CDS = any(feature_type == "CDS"),
      in_5UTR = any(feature_type %in% c("five_prime_utr", "five_prime_UTR")),
      in_3UTR = any(feature_type %in% c("three_prime_utr", "three_prime_UTR")),
      in_start_codon = any(feature_type == "start_codon"),
      in_stop_codon = any(feature_type == "stop_codon"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      desc(n_methods),
      CHR_original,
      POS
    )
  
} else {
  
  snp_feature_summary <- tibble(
    SNP_ID = character(),
    CHR_original = character(),
    CHR = character(),
    POS = numeric(),
    n_methods = numeric(),
    overlap_category = character(),
    feature_types = character(),
    gene_ids = character(),
    transcript_ids = character(),
    gene_names = character(),
    in_gene = logical(),
    in_transcript = logical(),
    in_exon = logical(),
    in_CDS = logical(),
    in_5UTR = logical(),
    in_3UTR = logical(),
    in_start_codon = logical(),
    in_stop_codon = logical()
  )
}

write_csv(
  snp_feature_summary,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_outlier_SNPs_feature_type_summary.csv")
  )
)

```

### 10.2.3. Classify each SNP into broad context

This simplifies the detailed feature annotation into broad classes

This tells you whether each SNP is:

CDS
UTR
exon_non_CDS
likely_intronic
other

```{r}
snp_context_summary <- snp_feature_summary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    broad_context = dplyr::case_when(
      in_CDS ~ "CDS",
      in_5UTR | in_3UTR ~ "UTR",
      in_exon ~ "exon_non_CDS",
      in_gene & !in_exon & !in_CDS & !in_5UTR & !in_3UTR ~ "likely_intronic",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  )

snp_context_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(broad_context, name = "n_snps") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_snps))

write_csv(
  snp_context_summary,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_outlier_SNPs_broad_context_summary.csv")
  )
)

```

# 11. Check the most important SNPs

This creates a selected table with the most relevant SNP-level annotation columns

```{r}
most_important_outlier_snps <- snp_context_summary %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_methods), broad_context, CHR_original, POS) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    SNP_ID,
    CHR_original,
    POS,
    n_methods,
    overlap_category,
    broad_context,
    feature_types,
    gene_ids,
    gene_names
  )

write_csv(
  most_important_outlier_snps,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_MOST_IMPORTANT_outlier_SNPs_selected_context_summary.csv")
  )
)
```

# 12. Prepare the IDs for `eggNOG`

`eggNOG` does not work directly from SNPs. It needs sequences, usually protein sequences

Which transcript IDs correspond to my candidate genes?

```{r}
# This converts the full GTF to a normal table
annotation_table <- as_tibble(annotation_gr) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

names(annotation_table)
table(annotation_table$type)

# Gene-to-transcript mapping from AND GTF
transcript_feature_types <- c("transcript", "mRNA")

# extracts transcript rows
gene_transcript_map <- annotation_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(type %in% transcript_feature_types) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::any_of(c(
      "gene_id",
      "transcript_id",
      "gene",
      "gene_name",
      "gene_biotype",
      "product",
      "description"
    ))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

write_csv(
  gene_transcript_map,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_gene_transcript_map_from_GTF.csv")
  )
)

# Add missing optional columns safely
# This part is a safety step
# This avoids errors in later mutate() steps
if (!"gene_name" %in% names(gene_transcript_map)) {
  gene_transcript_map$gene_name <- NA_character_
}

if (!"gene" %in% names(gene_transcript_map)) {
  gene_transcript_map$gene <- NA_character_
}

if (!"description" %in% names(gene_transcript_map)) {
  gene_transcript_map$description <- NA_character_
}

if (!"product" %in% names(gene_transcript_map)) {
  gene_transcript_map$product <- NA_character_
}

if (!"gene_biotype" %in% names(gene_transcript_map)) {
  gene_transcript_map$gene_biotype <- NA_character_
}

# Standardize gene/transcript map
# This creates a cleaned version

gene_transcript_map_clean <- gene_transcript_map %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_id = as.character(gene_id),
    transcript_id = as.character(transcript_id),
    
    gene_name_final = dplyr::coalesce(
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$gene_name), ""),
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$gene), ""),
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$gene_id), "")
    ),
    
    gene_description_final = dplyr::coalesce(
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$description), ""),
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$product), ""),
      dplyr::na_if(as.character(.data$gene_biotype), "")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(gene_id),
    gene_id != "",
    !is.na(transcript_id),
    transcript_id != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    gene_id = gene_id,
    transcript_id = transcript_id,
    gene_name = gene_name_final,
    gene_description = gene_description_final,
    gene_biotype = gene_biotype
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    gene_id,
    transcript_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

write_csv(
  gene_transcript_map_clean,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_gene_transcript_map_clean_from_GTF.csv")
  )
)

# Match candidate genes to transcript IDs
# Candidate gene X has transcript Y
# This is essential because eggNOG will annotate transcript/protein sequences, not the SNPs directly

candidate_gene_transcript_map <- candidate_genes_gene_level %>%
  dplyr::select(
    candidate_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gene_transcript_map_clean,
    by = c("candidate_gene_id" = "gene_id")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    candidate_gene_id,
    transcript_id
  )

write_csv(
  candidate_gene_transcript_map,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_gene_transcript_mapping.csv")
  )
)

# Create transcript ID list for `eggNOG`
# This is the input file used by your terminal `eggNOG` script
# It contains one transcript ID per line
# This file is used in terminal to extract only the proteins corresponding to candidate genes

candidate_transcript_ids <- candidate_gene_transcript_map %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(transcript_id)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(transcript_id != "") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(transcript_id) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(transcript_id)

write_tsv(
  candidate_transcript_ids,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_transcript_ids.txt")
  ),
  col_names = FALSE
)

# Diagnostics
candidate_gene_transcript_map %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_candidate_genes = dplyr::n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
    n_candidate_genes_with_transcript = dplyr::n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[!is.na(transcript_id)]),
    n_candidate_genes_without_transcript = dplyr::n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[is.na(transcript_id)]),
    n_candidate_transcripts = dplyr::n_distinct(transcript_id, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Check that the eggNOG input file was created
file.exists(
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_transcript_ids.txt")
  )
)

```

# 13. Read `eggNOG` output

This reads the main eggNOG output file

It also removes the # from the first column name and standardises all column names

```{r}
eggnog_file <- file.path(
  annotation_output_dir,
  "eggnog_candidate_genes",
  paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_genes_eggnog.emapper.annotations")
)

eggnog_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
  eggnog_file,
  comment = "##",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

names(eggnog_raw) <- names(eggnog_raw) %>%
  stringr::str_remove("^#") %>%
  janitor::make_clean_names()

eggnog <- eggnog_raw %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

glimpse(eggnog)
names(eggnog)
```

# 14. Check query column

This finds the `eggNOG` column containing the transcript/protein query ID

```{r}
query_candidates <- c(
  "query",
  "query_name",
  "query_seq",
  "x_query"
)

query_col <- query_candidates[query_candidates %in% names(eggnog)][1]

query_col

if (is.na(query_col)) {
  stop(
    "Could not identify query column in eggNOG output. Available columns are: ",
    paste(names(eggnog), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

eggnog %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(query_col)) %>%
  head()
```

# 15. Join `eggNOG` to candidate gene-transcript map

```{r}
eggnog_clean <- eggnog %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    eggnog_query = dplyr::all_of(query_col)
  )

glimpse(eggnog_clean)

# Check whether eggNOG query IDs match your transcript IDs

transcript_eggnog_overlap <- tibble(
  n_candidate_transcripts = dplyr::n_distinct(candidate_gene_transcript_map$transcript_id, na.rm = TRUE),
  n_eggnog_queries = dplyr::n_distinct(eggnog_clean$eggnog_query, na.rm = TRUE),
  n_matching_transcripts = length(intersect(
    na.omit(candidate_gene_transcript_map$transcript_id),
    na.omit(eggnog_clean$eggnog_query)
  ))
)

transcript_eggnog_overlap

# Join
# candidate gene → transcript ID → eggNOG annotation

candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog <- candidate_gene_transcript_map %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    eggnog_clean,
    by = c("transcript_id" = "eggnog_query")
  )

glimpse(candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog)

write_csv(
  candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog_annotation.csv")
  )
)

# Diagnostic summary
candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog %>%
  summarise(
    n_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
    n_candidate_transcripts = n_distinct(transcript_id),
    n_transcripts_with_eggnog_hit = n_distinct(transcript_id[!is.na(seed_ortholog)]),
    n_transcripts_without_eggnog_hit = n_distinct(transcript_id[is.na(seed_ortholog)])
  )

```

# 16. Join `eggNOG` to candidate SNP-gene table

This is the SNP-gene table plus functional annotation

```{r}
eggnog_annotation_columns <- c(
  "seed_ortholog",
  "evalue",
  "score",
  "egg_nog_ogs",
  "max_annot_lvl",

available_eggnog_annotation_columns <- eggnog_annotation_columns[

]

available_eggnog_annotation_columns

# Join eggNOG annotation to the candidate SNP-gene table
candidate_gene_table_with_eggnog <- candidate_gene_table_full %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    candidate_gene_transcript_eggnog %>%
      dplyr::select(

glimpse(candidate_gene_table_with_eggnog)
```

This is the main SNP/gene/transcript-level functional interpretation table

```{r}

interpretation_columns <- c(

candidate_gene_interpretation_table
```

# 18. Create gene-level `eggNOG` table

Final table for biological interpretation

```{r}

# One row per candidate gene-transcript annotation
candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level <- candidate_gene_interpretation_table %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    candidate_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name,
    candidate_gene_description,
    transcript_id,
    preferred_name,
    description,
    seed_ortholog,
    max_annot_lvl,
    cog_category,
    ec,
    kegg_ko,
    kegg_pathway,
    kegg_module
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_outlier_snps = n_distinct(SNP_ID),
    snps = paste(unique(SNP_ID), collapse = "; "),
    original_chromosomes = paste(unique(CHR_original), collapse = "; "),
    positions = paste(unique(POS), collapse = "; "),
    max_method_support = max(n_methods, na.rm = TRUE),
    overlap_categories = paste(unique(overlap_category), collapse = "; "),
    relation_types = paste(unique(relation_to_gene), collapse = "; "),
    min_distance_to_gene = min(distance_to_gene, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(max_method_support),
    dplyr::desc(n_outlier_snps),
    candidate_gene_id,
    transcript_id
  )

candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level

write_csv(
  candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level,
  file.path(
    annotation_output_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_FINAL_candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level_table.csv")
  )
)

# Diagnostic
candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
    n_transcripts = n_distinct(transcript_id),
    n_genes_with_eggnog_description = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[!is.na(description)]),
    n_genes_without_eggnog_description = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[is.na(description)]),
    n_genes_with_kegg_ko = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[!is.na(kegg_ko) & kegg_ko != "-"]),
    n_genes_with_kegg_pathway = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[!is.na(kegg_pathway) & kegg_pathway != "-"]),
    n_genes_with_cog = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id[!is.na(cog_category) & cog_category != "-"])
  )
```

# 19. Functional annotation plots

## 19.1 Create output directory

```{r}
functional_plot_dir <- file.path(
  annotation_output_dir,
  "functional_annotation_plots"
)

dir.create(functional_plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

functional_plot_dir
```

## 19.2 COG dictionary

```{r}
cog_labels <- c(
  "A" = "RNA processing and modification",
  "B" = "Chromatin structure and dynamics",
  "C" = "Energy production and conversion",
  "D" = "Cell cycle control, cell division, chromosome partitioning",
  "E" = "Amino acid transport and metabolism",
  "F" = "Nucleotide transport and metabolism",
  "G" = "Carbohydrate transport and metabolism",
  "H" = "Coenzyme transport and metabolism",
  "I" = "Lipid transport and metabolism",
  "J" = "Translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis",
  "K" = "Transcription",
  "L" = "Replication, recombination and repair",
  "M" = "Cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis",
  "N" = "Cell motility",
  "O" = "Posttranslational modification, protein turnover, chaperones",
  "P" = "Inorganic ion transport and metabolism",
  "Q" = "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis, transport and catabolism",
  "R" = "General function prediction only",
  "S" = "Function unknown",
  "T" = "Signal transduction mechanisms",
  "U" = "Intracellular trafficking, secretion, and vesicular transport",
  "V" = "Defense mechanisms",
  "W" = "Extracellular structures",
  "Y" = "Nuclear structure",
  "Z" = "Cytoskeleton"
)

cog_dictionary <- tibble(
  cog_category = names(cog_labels),
  cog_description = unname(cog_labels)
)

cog_dictionary
```

## 19.3. COG category summary table

```{r}
cog_long <- candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level %>%
  dplyr::select(
    candidate_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name,
    preferred_name,
    description,
    n_outlier_snps,
    max_method_support,
    cog_category
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(cog_category),
    cog_category != "-",
    cog_category != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cog_category = stringr::str_replace_all(cog_category, "\\s+", "")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(cog_category, sep = "") %>%
  dplyr::filter(cog_category != "") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    cog_dictionary,
    by = "cog_category"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cog_description = dplyr::if_else(
      is.na(cog_description),
      paste0("Unmapped COG category: ", cog_category),
      cog_description
    ),
    gene_label = dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(candidate_gene_name) & candidate_gene_name != "" ~ candidate_gene_name,
      !is.na(preferred_name) & preferred_name != "" ~ preferred_name,
      TRUE ~ candidate_gene_id
    )
  )

cog_long

# Summarise COG categories
cog_summary <- cog_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    cog_category,
    cog_description
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
    n_transcripts = n_distinct(preferred_name),
    mean_method_support = mean(max_method_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_method_support = max(max_method_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    genes = paste(sort(unique(candidate_gene_id)), collapse = "; "),
    gene_labels = paste(sort(unique(gene_label)), collapse = "; "),
    descriptions = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(description))), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(n_candidate_genes),
    cog_category
  )

cog_summary

write_csv(
  cog_summary,
  file.path(
    functional_plot_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_COG_category_summary.csv")
  )
)
```

## 19.4. COG bar plot

```{r}
if (nrow(cog_summary) > 0) {
  
  cog_barplot <- cog_summary %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      cog_description_wrapped = stringr::str_wrap(cog_description, width = 45),
      cog_description_wrapped = forcats::fct_reorder(
        cog_description_wrapped,
        n_candidate_genes
      )
    ) %>%
    ggplot(
      aes(
        x = n_candidate_genes,
        y = cog_description_wrapped
      )
    ) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey50") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = n_candidate_genes),
      hjust = -0.25,
      size = 3.2
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)),
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(species_name, " candidate genes: COG functional categories"),
      subtitle = "Descriptive summary of eggNOG COG annotations",
      x = "Number of candidate genes",
      y = "COG category"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  
  cog_barplot
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_COG_category_barplot.png")
    ),
    plot = cog_barplot,
    width = 10,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 400
  )
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_COG_category_barplot.pdf")
    ),
    plot = cog_barplot,
    width = 10,
    height = 7
  )
  
} else {
  message("No COG annotations available for plotting.")
}
```

## 19.5 COG bar plot with gene labels

```{r}
if (nrow(cog_summary) > 0) {
  
  cog_plot_table <- cog_summary %>%

      plot.margin = margin(5.5, 220, 5.5, 5.5)
    )
  
  cog_barplot_with_gene_names
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_COG_barplot_with_gene_names_and_functions.png")
    ),
    plot = cog_barplot_with_gene_names,
    width = 16,
    height = 8.5,
    dpi = 400
  )
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_COG_barplot_with_gene_names_and_functions.pdf")
    ),
    plot = cog_barplot_with_gene_names,
    width = 16,
    height = 8.5
  )
  
} else {
  message("No COG annotations available for gene-label plot.")
}
```

## 19.6 KEGG pathway summary

```{r}
kegg_gene_table <- candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level %>%
  dplyr::select(
    candidate_gene_id,
    candidate_gene_name,
    preferred_name,
    description,
    n_outlier_snps,
    max_method_support,
    kegg_pathway
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

kegg_long <- kegg_gene_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(kegg_pathway),
    kegg_pathway != "-",
    kegg_pathway != ""
  ) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(kegg_pathway, sep = ",") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    kegg_pathway = stringr::str_trim(kegg_pathway)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(kegg_pathway != "")

kegg_long

# KEGG diagnostic
kegg_annotation_diagnostic <- tibble(
  total_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level$candidate_gene_id),
  genes_with_kegg_pathway = n_distinct(kegg_long$candidate_gene_id),
  genes_without_kegg_pathway = total_candidate_genes - genes_with_kegg_pathway,
  total_kegg_pathway_terms = n_distinct(kegg_long$kegg_pathway)
)

kegg_annotation_diagnostic

write_csv(
  kegg_annotation_diagnostic,
  file.path(
    functional_plot_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_KEGG_pathway_annotation_diagnostic.csv")
  )
)

# Summarise KEGG pathways
kegg_summary <- kegg_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(kegg_pathway) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
    gene_ratio = n_candidate_genes / n_distinct(kegg_long$candidate_gene_id),
    mean_method_support = mean(max_method_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_method_support = max(max_method_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    genes = paste(sort(unique(candidate_gene_id)), collapse = "; "),
    gene_names = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(candidate_gene_name))), collapse = "; "),
    preferred_names = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(preferred_name))), collapse = "; "),
    descriptions = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(description))), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(n_candidate_genes),
    dplyr::desc(gene_ratio)
  )

kegg_summary

write_csv(
  kegg_summary,
  file.path(
    functional_plot_dir,
    paste0(species_prefix, "_KEGG_pathway_summary.csv")
  )
)

```

## 19.7 KEGG bubble plot

```{r}
top_n_pathways <- 20

kegg_summary_top <- kegg_summary %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(
    order_by = n_candidate_genes,
    n = top_n_pathways,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pathway_label = stringr::str_replace_all(kegg_pathway, "path:", ""),
    pathway_label = stringr::str_replace_all(pathway_label, "ko:", ""),
    pathway_label = stringr::str_wrap(pathway_label, width = 45),
    pathway_label = forcats::fct_reorder(pathway_label, gene_ratio)
  )

if (nrow(kegg_summary_top) > 0) {
  
  kegg_bubble_plot <- ggplot(
    kegg_summary_top,
    aes(
      x = gene_ratio,
      y = pathway_label,
      size = n_candidate_genes
    )
  ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.9, colour = "grey35") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = n_candidate_genes),
      hjust = -0.9,
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene count") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.25))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(species_name, " candidate genes: KEGG pathway representation"),
      subtitle = "Descriptive representation among KEGG-annotated candidate genes, not enrichment",
      x = "Gene ratio",
      y = "KEGG pathway"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10)
    )
  
  kegg_bubble_plot
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_KEGG_pathway_bubble_plot.png")
    ),
    plot = kegg_bubble_plot,
    width = 11,
    height = 8,
    dpi = 400
  )
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_KEGG_pathway_bubble_plot.pdf")
    ),
    plot = kegg_bubble_plot,
    width = 11,
    height = 8
  )
  
} else {
  message("No KEGG pathway annotations available for plotting.")
}

```

## 19.8 General KEGG KO/pathway/module representation

```{r}
required_pathway_cols <- c("kegg_ko", "kegg_pathway", "kegg_module")

if (all(required_pathway_cols %in% names(candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level))) {
  
  pathway_representation_long <- candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level %>%
    dplyr::select(
      candidate_gene_id,
      candidate_gene_name,
      n_outlier_snps,
      max_method_support,
      kegg_ko,
      kegg_pathway,
      kegg_module
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = c(kegg_ko, kegg_pathway, kegg_module),
      names_to = "annotation_type",
      values_to = "annotation_term"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(annotation_term),
      annotation_term != "-",
      annotation_term != ""
    ) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(annotation_term, sep = ",") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      annotation_term = stringr::str_trim(annotation_term),
      annotation_type = dplyr::recode(
        annotation_type,
        "kegg_ko" = "KEGG KO",
        "kegg_pathway" = "KEGG pathway",
        "kegg_module" = "KEGG module"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(annotation_term != "")
  
  pathway_representation_summary <- pathway_representation_long %>%
    dplyr::group_by(annotation_type, annotation_term) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_candidate_genes = n_distinct(candidate_gene_id),
      gene_ratio = n_candidate_genes / n_distinct(candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level$candidate_gene_id),
      mean_method_support = mean(max_method_support, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_outlier_snps = mean(n_outlier_snps, na.rm = TRUE),
      genes = paste(unique(candidate_gene_id), collapse = "; "),
      gene_names = paste(unique(na.omit(candidate_gene_name)), collapse = "; "),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      annotation_type,
      dplyr::desc(n_candidate_genes),
      dplyr::desc(gene_ratio)
    )
  
  pathway_representation_summary
  
  write_csv(
    pathway_representation_summary,
    file.path(
      functional_plot_dir,
      paste0(species_prefix, "_pathway_representation_summary.csv")
    )
  )
  
  top_n_per_type <- 10
  
  pathway_representation_top <- pathway_representation_summary %>%
    dplyr::group_by(annotation_type) %>%
    dplyr::slice_max(
      order_by = n_candidate_genes,
      n = top_n_per_type,
      with_ties = FALSE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      annotation_term = stringr::str_replace_all(annotation_term, "path:", ""),
      annotation_term = stringr::str_replace_all(annotation_term, "ko:", ""),
      annotation_term = stringr::str_replace_all(annotation_term, "md:", ""),
      annotation_term = stringr::str_wrap(annotation_term, width = 45),
      annotation_term = forcats::fct_reorder(annotation_term, gene_ratio)
    )
  
  if (nrow(pathway_representation_top) > 0) {
    
    pathway_representation_bubble_plot <- ggplot(
      pathway_representation_top,
      aes(
        x = gene_ratio,
        y = annotation_term,
        size = n_candidate_genes,
        colour = mean_method_support
      )
    ) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.9) +
      facet_grid(
        annotation_type ~ .,
        scales = "free_y",
        space = "free_y"
      ) +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene count") +
      scale_colour_gradient(
        low = "steelblue",
        high = "red3",
        name = "Mean method support"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(species_name, " candidate genes: functional representation"),
        subtitle = "KEGG KO, pathway, and module representation",
        x = "Gene ratio",
        y = "Annotation term"
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
      )
    
    pathway_representation_bubble_plot
    
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(
        functional_plot_dir,
        paste0(species_prefix, "_pathway_representation_bubble_plot.png")
      ),
      plot = pathway_representation_bubble_plot,
      width = 11,
      height = 10,
      dpi = 400
    )
    
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(
        functional_plot_dir,
        paste0(species_prefix, "_pathway_representation_bubble_plot.pdf")
      ),
      plot = pathway_representation_bubble_plot,
      width = 11,
      height = 10
    )
    
  } else {
    message("No KEGG KO/pathway/module annotations available for plotting.")
  }
  
} else {
  message("One or more KEGG columns are missing. Skipping pathway representation bubble plot.")
}

```

# 20. INFO

Main final files:

AND_FINAL_candidate_gene_interpretation_table.csv ( SNP/gene/transcript-level interpretation)

AND_FINAL_candidate_gene_eggnog_gene_level_table.csv (main biological interpretation of candidate genes)

AND_COG_category_summary.csv (summarise broad functional categories)

AND_KEGG_pathway_summary.csv (summarise KEGG pathway representation)

AND_pathway_representation_summary.csv (summarise KEGG KO, KEGG pathway, and KEGG module annotations together)
